newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil gets part of Malaysian oil project.
newsitem.headline: Statoil gets part of Malaysian oil project.

text.p: A letter of intent covering development of three Malaysian offshore fields has been secured by Statoil Shipping & Maritime Technology (SMT) in cooperation with local company Trenergy, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday.
The assignment, awarded by Malaysian state oil company Petronas -- relates to the Malong, Sotong and Anding discoveries, which are known collectively as Masa, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
The fields are due to be developed with Malaysia's first production ship, the Hitra. SMT will supply a loading buoy, production swivel and mooring systems to the project.
The fields are due to come on stream in the fourth quarter 1998. Statoil said Hitra was likely to pump about 45,000 barrels per day for at least a decade.
